references.text: Jesus says that with the measure you use, it will be measured to you—a principle that those who give will receive back, reflecting Luke 8:18 about how whoever has will be given more.
Matthew's parallel to the principle that whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they seem to have will be taken away. Almost identical wording in the parable discourse.
In the parable of the talents, Jesus repeats the same principle: whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
Mark's parallel where Jesus says 'Pay attention to what you hear' and that whoever has will be given more, while whoever does not have will lose even what they seem to have.
In the parable of the minas, Jesus states the same principle: whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
Describes those who hear the word and keep it in a noble and good heart—the context for the exhortation to pay attention to how one hears.
'Give to the wise, and he will become wiser still'—a wisdom saying from Proverbs expressing the same principle that whoever already has will be given more.
Jesus says that every branch that bears fruit, the Father cleanses so it may bear more fruit—an image of how whoever is already fruitful will be given even more.
James exhorts to be doers of the word, not merely hearers. Whoever looks into the perfect law of freedom and perseveres in it will be blessed—parallel to paying attention to how one hears.
The exhortation to pay all the more attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away from it—parallel to Jesus' warning about paying attention to how one hears.
